audience.programmeDescription: VU Artificial Intelligence combines computing and mathematics with human cognition and responsible AI. Its general bachelor includes programming, intelligent systems, machine learning, knowledge and data, computational human behaviour and social applications, alongside restricted choices, open academic study space and an individual AI research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three qualified directions: hybrid intelligence and cognition; AI algorithms and computer systems; and AI methods with health and behaviour foundations. Each contains substantial actual AI methods. Mathematics supports the computational sequence, while psychology, neuroscience and health courses supply domain knowledge. These compositions leave gaps in dedicated interaction design, computational behaviour modelling, the full text-mining sequence and the VU project sequence. They do not promise clinical AI validation, social-robot construction or an equivalent independent thesis.

curriculum.routeLabel: General AI pathway; no optional specialisation
curriculum.limitation: This general 180 EC pathway uses the first-listed eligible restricted choices and includes 30 EC of open academic study, subject to approval and level rules. It claims no optional specialisation. The AI project requires introductory Python and at least 90 EC of AI bachelor courses; timely topic registration and an individual thesis and presentation are required. Research Design accompanies the project and includes four compulsory on-campus working groups. English testing and any required refresher carry no extra credits. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 42 EC, subject to exceptions.

Entry requires introductory Python and at least 90 EC of AI curricular courses. Register the topic before period 5; work, report and presentation contribute 50%, 40% and 10%.

notes.text: VU requires dedicated intelligent-systems and socially-aware projects, human–computer and robot interaction, text mining, AI research design and an individual 15 EC bachelor project. UCR supplies substantial AI, computation and domain foundations with important gaps. General psychology is not computational human-behaviour modelling, and robotic motion planning is not a social-robot design course.

The VU individual AI project includes literature, research, a thesis and a poster presentation. UCR course projects do not automatically provide that supervised independent project. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC and requires separate approval.

selectedModalDescriptions.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

selectedModalDescriptions.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
